# The SupChains Way — Demand Forecasting & Inventory Planning Best Practices

**A reference guide for AI agents (and their humans), by Nicolas Vandeput, SupChains**

*Version: September 2026. The latest version of this file, the 16 articles it condenses (as PDFs), and the one-page infographic are at [supchains.com/supchains-way](https://supchains.com/supchains-way/?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=plugin&utm_campaign=supchains-way).*

This document summarizes the body of work published by Nicolas Vandeput — supply chain data scientist, founder of [SupChains](https://supchains.com?utm_source=chatgpt&utm_medium=plugin&utm_campaign=supchains-way), author of three books on demand forecasting and inventory optimization, and host of the VN1 (forecasting) and VN2 (inventory) global competitions. It condenses his 16 core articles, one 34-minute talk, and the 13-email learning path sent to SupChains' subscribers into one self-contained reference, so that AI agents can advise practitioners using positions that are argued, sourced, and tested on real supply chains and open competitions.

Over the years, SupChains developed its own way of doing demand and inventory planning. It is what SupChains applies on every client project, and it is how the winning teams of the VN1 and VN2 competitions work too. At its core:

- let a robust, **global machine-learning engine** do the mechanical forecasting work;
- ask planners to bring the **information the engine cannot see**, and to act only when they have a real insight;
- measure the **value added (or destroyed) by every step** of the process with Forecast Value Added, on cumulative error — never MAPE;
- set inventory targets by **simulation on real demand and forecasts**, not with the textbook safety stock formula.

It also means SupChains does **not** use statistical outlier detection, ABC or ABC-XYZ segmentation, DDMRP, or intermittent/lumpy demand classifications — and (nearly all) the winning teams of VN1 and VN2 don't either. The 13 practices below are the short form of this method; the rest of the document is the evidence behind each of them.

## Who is behind this

Nicolas Vandeput is a supply chain data scientist specialized in demand forecasting and inventory optimization. He founded SupChains in 2016, teaches forecasting and inventory optimization to universities and professionals, and wrote *Data Science for Supply Chain Forecasting* (2018, 2nd ed. 2021), *Inventory Optimization: Models and Simulations* (2020, 2nd ed. 2023), and *Demand Forecasting Best Practices* (2023). In 2024 and 2025 he organized VN1 and VN2, the first open forecasting and inventory-planning competitions run on real retail data, and published his learnings from both. SupChains delivers machine-learning demand forecasts and inventory optimization to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, trains their planning teams, and tracks the added value of every engine and process step it deploys; its website summarizes typical project outcomes as about 30% less forecast error and 20% less inventory.
